Nina / Diego — adding technical detail below (summarized for SIG entries). I'll attach the backup schedule and a replication diagram for context.

- Critical workloads: inference-serving GPU clusters (model servers), token/authorization service, and primary metadata DB (CockroachDB). Non-critical: analytics pipelines, batch feature stores.

- RPO:
  - Critical services: 15 minutes (continuous WAL + asynchronous cross-region replication).
  - Non-critical services: 24 hours (daily snapshots + incremental logs).

- RTO:
  - In-region failover (node/instance-level): target 15–30 minutes for transparent routing changes and autoscaling recovery.
  - Cross-region failover (warm standby): target 3 hours for warm-standby promotion, DNS TTLs and model cache warm-up included.
  - Cold-standby restore (rare): target 24 hours.

- Backups and retention:
  - Snapshot cadence: critical DBs: every 15 minutes (incremental snapshots), full snapshot nightly.
  - Object store backups (model artifacts): daily, retained 90 days by default (longer retention options available per contract).
  - Retention: default 90 days; archival to customer-controlled S3 possible for compliance needs.

- Encryption / KMS:
  - All backups encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS keys (AES-256 + Cloud KMS/HSM). Keys can be rotated per customer schedule.
  - In-transit: TLS 1.2+ between services and for cross-region replication.

- Failover approach:
  - Warm-standby architecture: secondary region runs a reduced fleet with continuous data replication (async with assured RPO for critical). Automated promotion uses routing policies in our smart router and optional health-check-based failover.

- DR tests:
  - Quarterly restore exercises for critical services; last full rehearsal: 2026-02-14 (log summary attached).
  - Automated smoke restores run monthly for a subset of customer tenants.

I've attached: backup-schedule.pdf and replication-diagram.png. Diego — I'll also add the restore-playbook to the shared drive and mark redactions for anything that shouldn't be shared publicly.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Principal Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Aaron / Nina — consolidated answers below and links to artifacts. I've zipped the final SIG BCDR bundle for your convenience.

1) Key management: By default we use customer-managed KMS keys when customers opt into BYOK. For new tenants, we recommend BYOK for PHI/scoped workloads; Redwood-managed keys are available if customers prefer simpler ops. We support AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and HSM-backed solutions for enterprise contracts.

2) One-page DR rehearsal summary: attached (short table). Quick callouts from 2026-02-14 rehearsal:
   - Planned failover start: 09:00 UTC; full service restore (customer-visible) achieved at 11:05 UTC -> effective RTO ~2h5m (within warm-standby target of up to 3 hours).
   - Issues: model cache warm-up longer than expected; we are improving pre-warming hooks to reduce this to under 30 minutes on next run.

3) SLA credits: Yes — SLA remedies are in our enterprise contract (section 4.2). For Dedicated and Private deployments we offer financial credits tied to monthly uptime and latency SLOs. For Hosted tenants we offer operational remediation paths; contractual SLAs are available for Enterprise plans. We can share the exact contract language under an NDA or during procurement.

4) Additional specifics to include in SIG:
   - RPO critical: 15 minutes; non-critical: 24 hours.
   - RTO in-region: 15–30 minutes; cross-region warm-standby: target 3 hours; cold-standby restore: 24 hours.
   - Retention: default 90 days; archival and longer retention configurable per account.
   - Encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit; customer-managed keys supported.
   - DR cadence: quarterly full rehearsals, monthly smoke restores.

Artifacts (shared):
- https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleShared/BCDR-artifacts (redacted runbook, rehearsal summary, restore-playbook PDF).
- DevOps runbook: https://app.redwoodinference.com/runbooks/EVW-2345-DR-RUNBOOK (access for Everwell team granted).
